question.leadin: This man was the first president of Gran Colombia, and he won the battles of Boyaca and Carabobo.
question.text: Name this South American leader known as "The Liberator."
question.answerHtml: Simón Bolívar [or Simón José Antonio de la Santísima Trinidad Bolívar Palacios Ponte y Blanco]
question.clue: This man, who wrote the Letter from Jamaica while in exile, issued the Decree of War to the Death during the Admirable campaign.

swap.leadin: Name these Latin American nations that were the site of twentieth-century violence.
swap.text: A CIA-backed 1973 coup in this nation led to the suicide of president Salvador Allende in Santiago's La Moneda Palace.
swap.clue: This country's Patria Vieja period of independence was ended at the Disaster of Rancagua.

question.leadin: During a coup, this leader committed suicide by AK-47 at the Palacio de La Moneda.
question.text: Name this socialist leader, who was replaced by the far-right dictator Augusto Pinochet as a result of that coup.
question.clue: This leader "Had to Die" according to an essay by Gabriel Garcia Marquez, and he likely died holding a sub-machine gun gifted to him by Fidel Castro.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about British prime minister Margaret Thatcher and education.
swap.text: Schoolteacher Diana Gould pressed Thatcher on the sinking of this country's ship General Belgrano during the Falklands War, which was fought between the UK and this country. Earlier, this country was led by Juan Peron.
swap.clue: In 1955 this nation's navy bombed its own Plaza de Mayo; the resulting military government later conducted the Dirty War against dissidents.

question.leadin: This leader introduced chewing gum to the United States while in exile there.
question.text: Name this leader who served as many as eleven terms as president of Mexico in the first half of the 19th century, a number that is debated due to his frequent use of puppet rulers between terms.
question.answerHtml: Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna [or Antonio de Padua María Severino López de Santa Anna y Pérez de Lebrón]
question.clue: While fighting a French blockade of his country's ports in the Pastry War, this leader gave a military burial to his amputated leg.

swap.text: Troops sent by this Cuban dictator participated in the Angolan Civil War on the side of the MPLA.
swap.clue: This leader tasked a fellow revolutionary with purging an army at La Cabana fortress.

question.leadin: In 2006 it elected its first female president, Michelle Bachelet.
question.text: Name this country which fought against Bolivia and Peru in the War of the Pacific, and which experienced an earthquake in Concepcion in 1570.
question.clue: The assassination of Orlando Letelier was accomplished in Washington DC, with US aid, by this country's DINA secret police as part of Operation Condor.

swap.leadin: A priest from this country documented military torture tactics during "Sunday Radio Sermons" that drew from his paper Orientacion.
swap.text: Name this country where Roberto D'Aubuisson ("dow-bwee-SOHN") ordered the killing of Archbishop Oscar Romero. This country fought a civil war with the FMLN.
swap.clue: The El Mozote massacre was a part of the "draining the sea" scorched earth tactics that this country's army used in a civil war against the FMLN, a party named for peasant leader Farabundo Marti.

question.leadin: On this holiday in 1647, people in Canterbury rioted on news that it was to be treated as any other working day with no sermon given.
question.text: Identify this holiday whose celebration was banned by Parliament in the mid-1640s.
question.clue: This date that alternately names the Baptist War led by deacon Samuel Sharpe in Jamaica.

swap.leadin: Bertha Lutz led a successful push for women's suffrage under this leader.
swap.text: Name this Brazilian dictator who stifled the power of "coffee and milk" era oligarchs after establishing the Estado Novo in 1937.
swap.clue: This leader first gained office after Washington Luis supported another man from his state as his successor, prompting a coup that ended the politics of coffee with milk.

question.leadin: Identify these figures from the history of.
question.text: He became 's first president upon its independence from the in 1901. Although he won a second term in 1905, he resigned the next year when rebellions broke out.

swap.leadin: A 30 for 30 documentary contrasts this man's life with that of a soccer player with the same last name who was gunned down after scoring an own goal.
swap.text: Name this former boss of the Medellin Cartel who was the best-known trafficker of cocaine until his 1993 death.
swap.clue: This man agreed to a period of nominal captivity at La Catedral prison in exchange for a deal preventing his extradition to the U.S.

question.leadin: Troops kidnapped victims and drowned them at the port of Montecristi during this event.
question.text: Name this 1937 event where tens of thousands were killed near the border of the Dominican Republic. Rafael Trujillo carried out this event named for a shibboleth that, if pronounced wrong, would result in execution.
question.clue: This event was followed the next year by a campaign called "el desalojo," or "the eviction," which forced thousands to flee from the Cibao region.

swap.text: This former dissident against the Brazilian junta ("HOON-tah"), who was tortured by its secret police, would later become president of Brazil. This leader was impeached and replaced with Michel Temer ("mee-SHELL TAY-mair") in 2016.
swap.clue: This economist and former left-wing president of Brazil was impeached in 2016 over concerns about budgetary irresponsibility and a scandal involving the state-run oil company Petrobras.

question.text: This term that refers to the period of domination of politics by sugar oligarchs during the Old Republic led to the Revolution of 1930 through the domination of the sugar industry in southern Brazilian states.
question.answerHtml: café com leite politics (accept coffee with milk politics)

swap.leadin: The Swiss-born Martin Schmid designed many of these locations.
swap.text: What places primarily in modern-day Paraguay were home to many Tupi and Chiquito people in the 17th and 18th centuries? They resisted slave raiders and enjoyed economic success before dying out in the 1760s.
swap.answerHtml: Jesuit reductions [or Jesuit missions; prompt on partial answers; prompt on Indian reductions]
swap.clue: This name for South American Jesuit missions that protected over one hundred thousand native Guarani from Portuguese bandeirantes, but forced them to give up most tribal traditions.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the dissemination of Rousseau in Spanish America.
question.text: Cecilio Baez's 1910 study of this dictator may have begun the common view that he sought to implement The Social Contract in practice. The doctorate of this first leader of independent Paraguay was actually in theology.
question.answerHtml: Doctor Francia [or José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia; prompt on El Supremo or Karai Guazu]

swap.text: After barely losing out at Cunindamarca, the Liberal forces were scattered by General Valencia in this twelve day battle in the coffee fields of Santander of May, 1900. It was the turning point in the War of a Thousand Days.

question.text: In 1825, this Argentine backed group led by Juan Lavalleja had steadily gained the support of ruler Uruguayans to throw out the Portuguese and dismantle the Cisplatine Republic.
question.answerHtml: Thirty Three Immortals [or Band of 33; or Los treinta y tres; accept equivalents]

swap.text: This man succeeded Mitre as the President of Argentina in 1868, and is best known for policies promoting education. He also wrote Facundo.
